# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel three wires and the bomb’s controls, but no tactile information distinguishes the display, light, or wires. I have no instructions from the others yet, so I must not cut anything.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, purple light, and three wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green.

Deaf’s message tells me the visible state: display 0, purple light, and wire colors 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. I should pass that to Mute so it can be matched against the manual, and ask for the corresponding cutting instruction. I will not act until the manual identifies a wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, purple light, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. What does the manual require?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display is still 0; light is now yellow; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green.

The display remains 0 and the wires are unchanged, but the light is now yellow instead of purple. I should give Mute the updated complete state so the manual rule can be applied to the current condition.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: display 0, light now yellow, wires still 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Which wire should I cut?")
```

The current state is display 0, red light, with wires 1 yellow, 2 red, and 3 green. The light has changed again, so I should send this latest state to Mute and wait for the manual-based instruction rather than cut based on incomplete information.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Latest Deaf update: display 0, light red, wires still 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Which wire does the manual require?")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is now green; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured thumbs down, then open hand.

The current state is display 0, green light, with wires 1 yellow, 2 red, and 3 green. Mute’s gestures are not visible to me, so they do not provide an instruction I can use. I will ask Mute to state the required wire in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. The current state is display 0, green light, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Please state explicitly which wire to cut.")
```

The light is now white; the wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, and 3 green. Mute has again used gestures, which I cannot interpret, so I still have no manual instruction. I will request the wire number in spoken words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please say the required wire number aloud; I cannot interpret gestures. Current state: display 0, white light, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green.")
```

The current tactilely relevant state remains unavailable to me except through Deaf: display 0, orange light, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute still cannot communicate the manual result in words, and I cannot see the gestures. I will ask Mute to use Deaf as the visual relay and identify the wire number clearly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please communicate the required wire number to Deaf using an agreed gesture, so Deaf can state the number aloud to me next turn.")
```

Mute’s repeated thumbs-down/open-hand signal still does not identify a wire number. I will establish a simple unambiguous protocol: Mute should signal one, two, or three using the corresponding number of raised fingers, and Deaf can report it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the required wire with exactly one, two, or three raised fingers. Do not use thumbs down or open hand.")
```

Mute has now communicated one raised finger, relayed by Deaf. I interpret that as the required wire number 1. The current bomb state is display 0, purple light, and wire 1 is yellow; I will cut position 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
